screens.name: Settings
screens.purpose: The app's single screen: guides the user through granting the two required system permissions, lets them customize each of the two overlay button styles (font, colors, gradient) and the shared text-length bounds, and shows a live preview of each style.
key_ui_elements: Required System Permissions card with an Overlay row and an Accessibility Service row, each showing a granted/not-granted status icon and an 'Open' button that deep-links to the matching system Settings screen

App Language picker: a row of chips ('System Default' plus each supported language in its own native name) that overrides the app's UI language independent of the device's system language, applied immediately
Min/Max text length fields that gate when the floating overlay buttons appear (shared by both styles)

Style 1 section: live preview, font picker (Sans Serif / Serif / Monospace / Cursive), an emoji badge picker (optional, tap-to-select from a small predefined palette plus a None option, rendered in the image's top-left corner), text/background color pickers (tap-to-select swatches from a small predefined palette, selected swatch shown with a checkmark), gradient toggle and gradient end-color picker — font size is not user-configurable; it is auto-computed from text length
Style 2 section: an identical set of controls, including its own emoji badge picker and color pickers, for the second overlay button's independent style

features.name: Floating Style Overlay Triggers
features.description: A background AccessibilityService watches the actively focused editable field system-wide and shows two small floating overlay buttons — one per configured style — whenever the typed text's trimmed length falls within the user-configured min/max bounds.
acceptance_criteria: Typing in any editable field in any app shows both overlay buttons once trimmed length is within [minTextLength, maxTextLength].
The overlay buttons never appear for an empty field, even if the user configures minTextLength down to 0.
The two buttons render with visually distinct backgrounds and are independently tappable, each triggering its own style's render.
Overlay buttons hide immediately when length falls back out of bounds or focus moves to a non-editable view.
Dragging either button moves both together as a single draggable pair, and the position reacts live to settings changes without restarting the app.
features.implementation_notes: TextMonitorAccessibilityService (AccessibilityService, @AndroidEntryPoint) listens for TYPE_VIEW_TEXT_CHANGED/TYPE_VIEW_FOCUSED, tracks the current AccessibilityNodeInfo + text, and delegates the length check to a pure TextLengthEvaluator.isWithinBounds() so the boundary logic is unit-testable outside the framework. isWithinBounds() requires trimmedLength > 0 in addition to the configured [minLength, maxLength] range, guaranteeing the overlay only shows once the user has actually entered text. OverlayWindowManager stacks two FrameLayout buttons (backgrounds bg_overlay_button / bg_overlay_button_secondary) inside one vertical LinearLayout container shown via a single WindowManager TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY addView/removeView; each button's icon is that style's own emoji (read fresh from primaryEmoji()/secondaryEmoji() at showOverlay() time), centered via a TextView layered over a generic ic_style_convert ImageView fallback shown only when the style's badge is blank, so the two icons occupy identical bounds regardless of which is visible; each button gets its own onClick callback (onPrimaryClicked/onSecondaryClicked) but shares one drag-listener instance so both move together. Style 1 renders with the collected TextStyleConfig; Style 2 renders with SecondaryStyleConfig.toRenderConfig(primaryConfig), which merges the secondary font/colors/gradient/emoji onto the primary config's shared paddingDp.

features.name: Styled Image Rendering
features.description: Renders the captured text into a fixed 512x512 PNG square using the current TextStyleConfig — font, text color, solid or 2-stop gradient background, padding, and an optional emoji badge — with the font size auto-computed to fill the square and the text centered both horizontally and vertically. The square always has sharp corners (no border radius).
acceptance_criteria: The rendered bitmap is always exactly 512x512, regardless of text length.
Long strings wrap across multiple lines without overflowing the bitmap bounds, and font size shrinks automatically to fit.
Line wrapping only breaks at whitespace between words, never in the middle of a word, for any text whose individual words fit within the padded content width.
Text is centered both horizontally and vertically within the square.
An invalid hex color string falls back to a default color instead of crashing.
When a style's emoji field is non-blank, that emoji is drawn as a badge in the image's top-left corner, on top of the main text; a blank emoji field draws no badge.
The emoji glyph renders as a proper glyph (color emoji on modern devices) rather than a tofu box, regardless of which of the four bundled fonts the style uses.
features.implementation_notes: ImageRenderer.renderBitmap() delegates to buildFittedLayout(), which binary-searches the largest text size (12px-320px) whose StaticLayout both fits the padded content area's height AND keeps every whitespace-delimited word's measured width within the content width — a height-only check would accept sizes that only 'fit' by letting Android's line breaker split an overlong word mid-way, since the breaker forcibly wraps any word wider than the line rather than overflowing it. The chosen-size StaticLayout is then drawn centered onto a fixed 512x512 Canvas-backed Bitmap with a solid or LinearGradient square background (no rounded corners — config.cornerRadiusDp is no longer read). fontSizeSp has been removed entirely from TextStyleConfig, SettingsRepository, and the Settings UI, since font size is now always auto-computed. If config.emoji is non-blank, drawEmojiBadge() draws it last (on top of the main text) near the top-left corner using Typeface.DEFAULT rather than the style's own FontChoice — Android resolves emoji code points through the system-wide font fallback chain regardless of typeface family, so this reliably reaches the system's (vector/COLRv1 on modern devices) color emoji font instead of the four bundled type families needing their own emoji glyph coverage. generateStyledImageUri() writes the PNG to cacheDir/images and returns a FileProvider content URI. Rendering itself supports any Unicode script via Android's system font fallback (same mechanism the emoji badge uses) and lays out RTL scripts correctly via StaticLayout's default FIRSTSTRONG_LTR direction heuristic; the one known limitation is that the widest-word safety check splits on whitespace, so scripts without inter-word spaces (CJK, Thai, Lao, Khmer) can render at a smaller-than-optimal auto-fit size — see doc/i18n.md for the full analysis and the proper fix (Unicode line-break analysis instead of a whitespace split).

features.name: Clipboard Copy & Field Clear
features.description: Tapping either overlay button copies that button's rendered image to the system clipboard as an image/png ClipData and clears the original text field, so the user can immediately paste the styled image in place of what they typed.
acceptance_criteria: After tapping either overlay button, the system clipboard holds a ClipData whose item URI resolves to image/png, rendered with the tapped button's own style.
The originating text field is cleared via ACTION_SET_TEXT immediately after the copy.
A short confirmation Toast appears telling the user to paste.
features.implementation_notes: ClipboardManagerHelper.copyImageToClipboard() uses ClipData.newUri(contentResolver, label, uri) so the MIME type is resolved from FileProvider's own getType(). TextMonitorAccessibilityService.handleStyleButtonPressed(renderConfig) is shared by both buttons' click callbacks — each passes its own resolved TextStyleConfig — then calls AccessibilityNodeInfo.performAction(ACTION_SET_TEXT, empty string) on the tracked node.

features.name: Guided Permission Setup
features.description: The Settings screen live-checks both required permissions (SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW via Settings.canDrawOverlays, the accessibility service via AccessibilityManager.getEnabledAccessibilityServiceList) on every onResume, and deep-links straight to the matching system Settings screen for whichever is missing.
acceptance_criteria: Returning to the app after granting a permission in system Settings updates that row to 'Granted' without needing to relaunch the app.
Tapping 'Open' on the overlay row launches ACTION_MANAGE_OVERLAY_PERMISSION scoped to this app's package.
Tapping 'Open' on the accessibility row launches ACTION_ACCESSIBILITY_SETTINGS.
features.implementation_notes: PermissionUtils centralizes both live checks. MainActivity re-checks both in a DefaultLifecycleObserver.onResume() and triggers Play's In-App Review flow (InAppReviewHelper) the first time both permissions transition from not-fully-granted to fully-granted — a genuine positive completion point.

features.name: Live Style Preview & Customization
features.description: Every style control across both Style 1 and Style 2 sections (font, emoji badge, text/background/gradient color, gradient toggle) plus the shared min/max length bounds persists to DataStore and immediately re-renders that style's live preview bitmap of sample text so the user sees the effect of a change before it's ever used on real typed text.
acceptance_criteria: Changing any Style 1 or Style 2 control updates that style's own live preview image within one recomposition, without a manual 'apply' step.
Settings for both styles persist independently across app restarts.

Text, background, and gradient end colors are each chosen by tapping a swatch from a small predefined palette, so every persisted color value is always a valid hex string — there is no free-text color entry or invalid-color state to show.
features.implementation_notes: SettingsRepository wraps a single Preferences DataStore (`user_settings`) exposing TextStyleConfig (Style 1) and SecondaryStyleConfig (Style 2, under style2_* keys) as separate Flows; SettingsViewModel exposes each as its own StateFlow via stateIn(WhileSubscribed(5000)). SettingsScreen's LivePreview composable calls ImageRenderer.renderBitmap() on Dispatchers.Default inside produceState(config) and renders the result via Image(bitmap.asImageBitmap()) — called once per style, with Style 2's preview built via SecondaryStyleConfig.toRenderConfig(primaryConfig). The emoji field is a tap-to-select EmojiPicker (a FlowRow of EmojiChoiceChip boxes) over a fixed EMOJI_BADGE_CHOICES palette of 17 popular, category-diverse emoji plus a None chip (rendered at the same glyph size as the emoji choices) that sets emoji to blank — not a free-text field — so the persisted emoji string is always either blank or one of the palette entries. Text/background/gradient-end colors are each a tap-to-select ColorPicker (a FlowRow of circular ColorSwatch boxes, selected swatch marked with a checkmark whose black/white tint is chosen by isLightColor() luminance) over a fixed COLOR_PALETTE of 16 hex colors — not a free-text hex field — so the persisted color hex is always one of the palette entries.

features.name: Multi-language UI Support
features.description: All UI chrome (permission copy, section titles, field labels, the Toast, font names) is externalized to string resources and translated into five languages beyond the English default (Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Hindi). An App Language picker on the Settings screen lets the user override the app's display language independent of the device's system language; the default 'System Default' option automatically follows whichever of the device's configured languages the app has a translation for, falling back to English otherwise — so language detection is Android's own resource-qualifier resolution, not custom logic.
acceptance_criteria: With no override selected, the app's UI language automatically matches the device's system language when a translation exists, and falls back to English otherwise, with no user action required.

Selecting a specific language in the App Language picker immediately re-renders the entire Settings screen in that language and persists the choice across app restarts, independent of the device's system language.
Selecting 'System Default' clears the override and reverts to automatic system-language matching.

All screen text — permission copy, section titles, field labels, button text, the copied-image confirmation Toast, and the four font names — is translated in every supported language; no hardcoded English string remains outside of the rendered sample preview text.
features.implementation_notes: res/values/strings.xml holds the English defaults; res/values-{es,fr,de,pt,hi}/strings.xml hold full translations, selected automatically by Android's locale-qualified resource resolution. FontChoice's label field became a @StringRes labelRes so font names localize too. LanguagePicker (SettingsScreen.kt) offers 'System Default' plus each supported language in its own native name; on API 33+ it reads/writes the override via Context.getSystemService(LocaleManager::class.java).applicationLocales directly (the same mechanism the OS's own per-app language settings use), with androidx.appcompat's AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales() as the pre-33 fallback — then calls Activity.recreate() itself since MainActivity is a plain ComponentActivity, not AppCompatActivity, so it doesn't get AppCompat's automatic recreation. AndroidManifest declares android:localeConfig="@xml/locales_config" (listing en/es/fr/de/pt/hi) so Android 13+'s own system-level per-app language settings page also lists this app, and a manifest-declared androidx.appcompat.app.AppLocalesMetadataHolderService with autoStoreLocales=true meta-data is required for AppCompatDelegate's static API to have a valid Application context to act on — omitting it makes setApplicationLocales() a silent no-op.

non_goals: No custom Input Method (IME) / system keyboard in this version — text is styled and cleared in place via AccessibilityService, not typed through a replacement keyboard.
No arbitrary number of saved style presets or a style gallery — there are exactly two fixed style slots (Style 1 / Style 2), each edited directly in Settings and each backing its own overlay button.
No in-app purchases, ads, or any billing integration — the app is entirely free with no monetization.
No handwriting font creation — only the four bundled system type families (Sans Serif, Serif, Monospace, Cursive) are offered.
No cloud backend, accounts, or sync — all settings live in local DataStore on the one device.
No app-specific one-tap share target (e.g. WhatsApp) — the styled image is placed on the system clipboard for the user to paste anywhere themselves.

steps: Call TextLengthEvaluator.isWithinBounds with lengths below, at, and above the configured min/max bounds.
Call it again with trimmedLength = 0 and minLength = 0.
test_plan.expected: Lengths strictly below minLength or strictly above maxLength return false; lengths equal to either bound or in between return true. A trimmedLength of 0 always returns false, even when minLength is 0.

test_plan.scenario: Rendered bitmap is always a fixed 512x512 square
steps: Render a short string and a long multi-sentence string with the same TextStyleConfig via ImageRenderer.renderBitmap on a connected device.
Compare the resulting bitmap dimensions.
test_plan.expected: Both the short and long string bitmaps are exactly 512x512, regardless of text length.

test_plan.scenario: Line wrapping never breaks a word mid-way
steps: Build the fitted StaticLayout (via ImageRenderer.buildFittedLayout) for a multi-word sentence long enough to wrap across several lines.
For each line break, check whether the character immediately before and after the break are both non-whitespace.
test_plan.expected: Every line break falls on whitespace between words; no line ends mid-word.

test_plan.scenario: Invalid hex colors fall back instead of crashing
steps: Render text with a TextStyleConfig whose textColorHex and backgroundColorHex are not valid hex strings.
test_plan.expected: Rendering completes and returns a non-empty bitmap instead of throwing.

test_plan.scenario: Emoji badge renders without breaking the fixed square
steps: Render the same text with a TextStyleConfig whose emoji is a non-blank string, and again with emoji blank.
test_plan.expected: Both renders succeed and return an exact 512x512 bitmap; the non-blank case has a visible glyph badge in the top-left corner, the blank case has none.

steps: Launch MainActivity via ActivityScenario so the process holds window focus.
From inside the resumed Activity, render an image and call ClipboardManagerHelper.copyImageToClipboard.
Read back ClipboardManager.primaryClip from the same focused Activity.
test_plan.expected: The primary clip's item URI matches the copied URI and its MIME type is image/png.

test_plan.scenario: App Language override applies immediately and persists
steps: Open Settings with the device's system language set to English and no override selected.
Tap a non-English language chip (e.g. Español) in the App Language picker.
Force-close and relaunch the app.
Tap 'System Default' to clear the override.
test_plan.expected: The whole Settings screen re-renders in the selected language immediately after tapping its chip; the override survives the relaunch; tapping 'System Default' reverts the UI to the device's system language (English).

steps: Grant both the overlay and accessibility permissions, confirm both overlay buttons appear while typing.
Revoke one permission from system Settings, return to the app.
test_plan.expected: The revoked permission's row reverts to 'not granted' on the very next onResume, and the overlay buttons stop appearing until it's re-granted.

test_plan.scenario: Two overlay buttons with independent styles
steps: Set clearly different fonts/colors for Style 1 and Style 2 in Settings.
Type qualifying text in a monitored field and observe both floating buttons.
Drag one of the buttons and confirm both move together as a pair.
Tap the Style 1 button, paste, then repeat typing and tap the Style 2 button, paste.
test_plan.expected: Both buttons appear together and stay paired while dragging; pasting after the Style 1 tap shows an image in Style 1's look, and pasting after the Style 2 tap shows an image in Style 2's distinct look.

fields.name: font
fields.notes: maps to an Android generic Typeface family name

fields.name: backgroundColorHex
fields.notes: solid color, or gradient start color

fields.name: minTextLength
fields.notes: default 3 — overlay trigger lower bound, shared by both style buttons

fields.name: maxTextLength
fields.notes: default 280 — overlay trigger upper bound, shared by both style buttons

fields.name: emoji
fields.notes: default "✨" — optional badge drawn in the image's top-left corner; blank means no badge

fields.name: font
fields.notes: default SERIF, independent of the primary style's font

fields.name: backgroundColorHex
fields.notes: default #F5E9DA — solid color, or gradient start color

fields.name: emoji
fields.notes: default "🎨" — optional badge, independent of the primary style's emoji

data_model.notes: Backs the second overlay button. Only visual fields — paddingDp, minTextLength, and maxTextLength are borrowed from TextStyleConfig via SecondaryStyleConfig.toRenderConfig(base) when rendering.

libraries.purpose: Android Kotlin extensions and compatibility helpers
Per-app language override (AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales) for the App Language picker
Local key-value storage for the one active TextStyleConfig
Coroutines for DataStore flows and the accessibility service's settings collector
Dependency injection into the Application, Activity, and AccessibilityService
Play In-App Review prompt after first successful permission setup

positioning: Type anywhere — any app, any field — and turn what you typed into a beautifully styled image with one tap on a small floating button, ready to paste right back in.

design_system.typography: Google Fonts 'Fraunces' (serif, expressive) for in-app headings/branding, Material 3 default type scale (Roboto Flex) for all other UI chrome and body text — never used for the rendered style output itself, which always uses the user's selected style font.
design_system.theme_notes: Dark mode follows the system default: light theme uses background #F7F5FF / surface #FFFFFF / on-background #1C1B1F; dark theme uses background #16151F / surface #201F2C / on-background #E7E1FF.

store_listing.title: InkSend: Style Any Text
store_listing.icon_prompt: Create a 1024x1024 Android app icon for InkSend, a text-styling utility app. Rounded-square adaptive icon style, indigo background (#5B47E0), a simple white fountain-pen nib icon with a short flowing ink stroke. Flat vector design, high contrast, no text, no brand logos, no photorealistic elements.
store_listing.long_description:
InkSend turns anything you type, in any app, into a beautifully styled image — your choice of font, text color, background, and a little emoji badge — ready to paste back in with one tap.

Just start typing in any text field. Once your message is long enough, two small floating buttons appear, one for each of your two saved styles. Tap either one, and InkSend renders your exact words as a styled image in that look, copies it to your clipboard, and clears the field — so a long-press and Paste (or your keyboard's clipboard suggestion) drops the image right back in.

Customize both styles from one simple settings screen: font, an optional emoji badge, text color, background color or gradient, and exactly which text lengths should trigger the buttons — with a live preview of each style as you go. Font size always auto-fits your text, so there's nothing to fiddle with.

Everything happens on your device. No account, no ads, no subscription — InkSend is completely free.
store_listing.short_description: Style any text you type and paste it back in as an image — free, no ads, no account.

project_context: This spec describes an independent, alternative Android app you are building from scratch to compete with an existing incumbent app on Google Play — not a modification, clone, or reskin of the incumbent's own code, assets, or branding. Use the incumbent only as a market reference (via the report data below), and design working_name/package_id/store_listing/design_system so the result is clearly its own product.
build_instructions:
chmod +x ./gradlew
./gradlew clean
./gradlew testDebugUnitTest
./gradlew connectedDebugAndroidTest
keytool -genkeypair -v -keystore inksend-upload.jks -storetype JKS -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 -alias upload -dname "CN=InkSend Upload,O=AppyFYI,C=US" -storepass changeit -keypass changeit
RELEASE_STORE_FILE="$PWD/inksend-upload.jks" RELEASE_STORE_PASSWORD="changeit" RELEASE_KEY_ALIAS="upload" RELEASE_KEY_PASSWORD="changeit" ./gradlew bundleRelease
